extracted.intended_audience: authors submitting NLP research to ACL/ARR (conference/journal) for peer review
extracted.subtask_description: A required checklist for NLP paper submissions to ACL/ARR to encourage responsible research practices covering ethics, societal impact, artifact documentation, experiments, human subjects, and AI assistant use. Authors must indicate sections or justify negative answers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to ACL code of ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of the ACL are responsible for adhering to the ACL code of ethics. The ARR Responsible NLP Research checklist is designed to encourage best practices for responsible research, addressing issues of research ethics, societal impact and reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please read the Responsible NLP Research checklist guidelines for information on how to answer these questions. Note that not answering positively to a question is not grounds for rejection. All supporting evidence can appear either in the main paper or the supplemental material. For each question, if you answer Yes, provide the section number; if you answer No, provide a justification. Please do not modify, reorder, delete or add questions, question options or other wording of this document.

rubrics_metrics.name: A1: Discussion of limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you discuss the limitations of your work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you answer Yes, provide the section number; if you answer No, provide a justification. (Answer options: Yes / No / N/A; provide 'Section or Justification')

rubrics_metrics.name: A2: Discussion of potential risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you discuss any potential risks of your work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you answer Yes, provide the section number; if you answer No, provide a justification. (Answer options: Yes / No / N/A; provide 'Section or Justification')

rubrics_metrics.name: A3: Abstract and introduction summarize main claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Do the abstract and introduction summarize the paper’s main claims?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you answer Yes, provide the section number; if you answer No, provide a justification. (Answer options: Yes / No / N/A; provide 'Section or Justification')

rubrics_metrics.name: B: Use or creation of scientific artifacts (gating)
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you use or create scientific artifacts? If you answer Yes, answer the questions below; if you answer No, you can skip the rest of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer Yes/No for whether artifacts were used/created. If yes, respond to B1–B6 with section numbers or justifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: B1: Citation of artifact creators
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you cite the creators of artifacts you used?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you answer Yes, provide the section number; if you answer No, provide a justification. (Yes / No / N/A; 'Section or Justification')

rubrics_metrics.name: B2: Discussion of license/terms for artifacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you discuss the license or terms for use and/or distribution of any artifacts?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you answer Yes, provide the section number; if you answer No, provide a justification. State licenses/terms and how they affect use/distribution. (Yes / No / N/A)

rubrics_metrics.name: B3: Intended use and compatibility with original access conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you discuss if your use of existing artifact(s) was consistent with their intended use, provided that it was specified? For the artifacts you create, do you specify intended use and whether that is compatible with the original access conditions (in particular, derivatives of data accessed for research purposes should not be used outside of research contexts)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you answer Yes, provide the section number; if you answer No, provide a justification. Explain intended uses and compatibility with access conditions; note restrictions on derivatives of research-only data.

rubrics_metrics.name: B4: Data content checks and anonymization
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you discuss the steps taken to check whether the data that was collected/used contains any information that names or uniquely identifies individual people or offensive content, and the steps taken to protect / anonymize it?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you answer Yes, provide the section number; if you answer No, provide a justification. Describe checks for PII/offensive content and anonymization/protection procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: B5: Documentation of artifacts' coverage and demographics
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you provide documentation of the artifacts, e.g., coverage of domains, languages, and linguistic phenomena, demographic groups represented, etc.?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you answer Yes, provide the section number; if you answer No, provide a justification. Provide documentation describing domains, languages, phenomena, and demographic representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: B6: Reporting dataset statistics and splits
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you report relevant statistics like the number of examples, details of train/test/dev splits, etc. for the data that you used/created?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you answer Yes, provide the section number; if you answer No, provide a justification. Report counts, split details, and other relevant dataset statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: C: Computational experiments (gating)
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you run computational experiments? If you answer Yes, answer the questions below; if you answer No, you can skip the rest of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer Yes/No about running experiments. If yes, respond to C1–C4 with section numbers or justifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: C1: Model size, compute budget, and infrastructure reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you report the number of parameters in the models used, the total computational budget (e.g., GPU hours), and computing infrastructure used?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you answer Yes, provide the section number; if you answer No, provide a justification. Report parameter counts, total compute (GPU hours) and hardware/cloud infrastructure details.

rubrics_metrics.name: C2: Experimental setup and hyperparameter reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you discuss the experimental setup, including hyperparameter search and best-found hyperparameter values?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you answer Yes, provide the section number; if you answer No, provide a justification. Describe search procedures and report best hyperparameter settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: C3: Descriptive statistics and transparency of reported runs
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you report descriptive statistics about your results (e.g., error bars around results, summary statistics from sets of experiments), and is it transparent whether you are reporting the max, mean, etc. or just a single run?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you answer Yes, provide the section number; if you answer No, provide a justification. Report error bars, summary stats across runs and clarify whether reported numbers are max/mean/single-run.

rubrics_metrics.name: C4: Reporting implementation and package settings
rubrics_metrics.description: If you used existing packages (e.g., for preprocessing, for normalization, or for evaluation), did you report the implementation, model, and parameter settings used (e.g., NLTK, Spacy, ROUGE, etc.)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you answer Yes, provide the section number; if you answer No, provide a justification. List packages/libraries and their used settings to enable reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: D: Human annotators / human subjects research (gating)
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you use human annotators (e.g., crowdworkers) or research with human subjects? If you answer Yes, answer the questions below; if you answer No, you can skip the rest of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer Yes/No about human subjects. If yes, respond to D1–D5 with section numbers or justifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: D1: Full text of participant instructions and risk disclaimers
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you report the full text of instructions given to participants, including e.g., screenshots, disclaimers of any risks to participants or annotators, etc.?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you answer Yes, provide the section number; if you answer No, provide a justification. Include full instructions, screenshots, and any risk disclaimers.

rubrics_metrics.name: D2: Recruitment and payment details
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you report information about how you recruited (e.g., crowdsourcing platform, students) and paid participants, and discuss if such payment is adequate given the participants’ demographic (e.g., country of residence)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you answer Yes, provide the section number; if you answer No, provide a justification. Describe recruitment channels, payment amounts, and adequacy relative to participants' demographics.

rubrics_metrics.name: D3: Consent and explanation of data use
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you discuss whether and how consent was obtained from people whose data you’re using/curating (e.g., did your instructions explain how the data would be used)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you answer Yes, provide the section number; if you answer No, provide a justification. Describe consent procedures and what participants/data subjects were told about data use.

rubrics_metrics.name: D4: Ethics review board approval or exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: Was the data collection protocol approved (or determined exempt) by an ethics review board?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you answer Yes, provide the section number; if you answer No, provide a justification. State IRB/ethics approval or exemption details.

rubrics_metrics.name: D5: Demographic and geographic characteristics of annotators
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you report the basic demographic and geographic characteristics of the annotator population that is the source of the data?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you answer Yes, provide the section number; if you answer No, provide a justification. Report annotator demographics and geographic distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: E: Use of AI assistants (gating)
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you use AI assistants (e.g., ChatGPT, Copilot) in your research, coding, or writing? If you answer Yes, answer the question below; if you answer No, you can skip the rest of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer Yes/No regarding use of AI assistants. If yes, respond to E1 with section number or justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: E1: Disclosure of AI assistant use
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you include information about your use of AI assistants?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you answer Yes, provide the section number; if you answer No, provide a justification. Disclose how AI assistants were used in research, coding, or writing.
